structure: Part 4 read, in full, the commodity section of the high-risk plants set in repos/trade-imports-plants-frontend: the commodity-type feature folder (page.js, controller.js, template.njk, evaluation.js, copy/copy.en.js, copy/copy.cy.js, commodity-type.fit.spec.js; the copy.test.js and controller.test.js unit tests were listed but are out of scope by the partition), the commodities group (page.js, fields.js, line-form.js, links.js, entry-index.js, evaluation.js, list/list.controller.js, list/list.njk, details/details.controller.js, details/details.njk, copy/copy.en.js, copy/copy.cy.js, fit/list.fit.spec.js, fit/details.fit.spec.js, fit/axe.js), the set-owned commodity vocabulary services/commodities/index.js, and obligations/sections/commodity.js. Two values the commodity-type hints quote were looked up by grep in features/timing-windows.js (2 and 4 days), and the shared save-action labels and the 'About the consignment' caption were looked up in shared/copy.en.js and flow/section-captions/copy/copy.en.js. It covers three pages, all under the 'About the consignment' caption: the commodity type question (/notifications/{journeyId}/commodity-type, the notification's entry page), the commodities list (/notifications/{journeyId}/commodities, a table of saved lines with Change and Remove, which redirects to the entry sub-page when empty), and the commodity details entry sub-page (/notifications/{journeyId}/commodities/details, optionally ?index=N), which asks the category first, saves it, then reveals the per-line fields the category asks for. It also covers the commodity data the service hard-codes (3 types, 9 categories, 15 genera, the per-category field map and the origin constraints the origin page applies), the 13 obligations of the commodity section, and every test in the three fit specs (15, 11 and 18 tests). Claims run page by page: commodity type (001-034), list (035-066), details (067-140), service data (141-153), obligations (154-166), then gaps (167-170).

The genus must be one of the genera the line's category allows; otherwise the error is 'Select the genus'.
Plants for planting and trees for planting lines offer all fifteen genera; hardwood lines offer only Castanea, Fraxinus and Platanus.

Genus options are shown with scientific and common name: 'Castanea (sweet chestnut)', 'Cedrus (cedar)', 'Coffea (coffee)', 'Fraxinus (ash)', 'Lavandula (lavender)', 'Nerium oleander (oleander)', 'Olea europaea (olive)', 'Picea (spruce)', 'Pinus (pine)', 'Platanus (plane)', 'Polygala myrtifolia (myrtle-leaf milkwort)', 'Prunus (plums, cherry etc)', 'Quercus (oak)', 'Salvia rosmarinus (rosemary)', 'Ulmus (elm)'.
claims.quote: Castanea: 'Castanea (sweet chestnut)', ... Prunus: 'Prunus (plums, cherry etc)', ... Ulmus: 'Ulmus (elm)'

claims.statement: The commodity vocabulary (types, categories, genera, which fields each category asks for, origin constraints) is hard-coded in the plants frontend's own set-owned service, not fetched from MDM or reference data.
claims.quote:
/**
 * The set-owned commodity vocabulary.
claims.note: Every list in the file is an Object.freeze literal, and the file makes no call out. Relevant to the goal's 'commodities come from MDM' block.

claims.statement: The commodity service holds values only; every label and hint a page shows for a value is copy in the feature that renders it.
claims.quote:
The service holds values, never the words a page shows for them: a label or
 * a hint is a copy leaf in the feature that renders it.

claims.statement: There are nine categories of goods, offered in this order: seed-potatoes, ware-potatoes, plants-for-planting, trees-for-planting, conifer-wood-with-bark, conifer-wood-without-bark, cut-coniferous-trees, hardwood-round-surface, hardwood-chips.
claims.quote:
const CATEGORIES = Object.freeze([
  SEED_POTATOES,
  WARE_POTATOES,
  PLANTS_FOR_PLANTING,
  TREES_FOR_PLANTING,
  CONIFER_WOOD_WITH_BARK,
  CONIFER_WOOD_WITHOUT_BARK,
  CUT_CONIFEROUS_TREES,
  HARDWOOD_ROUND_SURFACE,
  HARDWOOD_CHIPS
])

claims.statement: The nine categories partition by commodity type, so each category belongs to exactly one type.
claims.quote:
// The nine categories partition by commodity type, so changing the type of a
// notification that already holds lines can keep none of them.

claims.statement: The genus list is the fifteen entries of regulation 26(1)(a), in its order (Castanea, Cedrus, Coffea, Fraxinus, Lavandula, Nerium oleander, Olea europaea, Picea, Pinus, Platanus, Polygala myrtifolia, Prunus, Quercus, Salvia rosmarinus, Ulmus); four are species rather than genera, as the regulation lists them.
claims.quote:
// The fifteen entries of reg 26(1)(a). Four are species rather than genera;
// the regulation lists them that way and so does this list.

claims.statement: Seed potatoes carry no origin narrowing: every country the origin block offers is acceptable for them (reg 24A(1)(a), the whole Common SPS Area).
claims.quote:
A category the list never names — seed potatoes,
 * scoped by reg 24A(1)(a) to the whole Common SPS Area — narrows nothing

claims.statement: When a consignment breaks more than one origin constraint, the origin page reports the narrowest: ware potatoes first, then conifer wood without bark, then EU member states.
claims.quote:
The order is the order the origin page reports a failure in: a consignment
 * that breaks more than one constraint is told about the narrowest.

claims.statement: The same category-per-field list both scopes each per-line obligation and decides which fields the details page renders, so the page and the model cannot disagree.
claims.quote:
One list per field, read twice: the obligation's `applyTo` gate scopes the
 * field to these categories, and the entry page renders exactly the fields
 * whose list holds the chosen category.

claims.statement: Asking a lookup for an unknown commodity type, category or field returns an empty list rather than an error.
claims.quote:
Object.hasOwn(CATEGORIES_BY_COMMODITY_TYPE, commodityType)
    ? CATEGORIES_BY_COMMODITY_TYPE[commodityType]
    : EMPTY

claims.statement: Obligation commodityType: the notification's commodity type is mandatory.
Obligation commodityLines: a notification must hold at least one commodity line, with the error code obligation.commodityLines.atLeastOne; it is a structural group, always in scope.
Obligation category: every commodity line must have a category, and it is the gate every other per-line field reads.
Obligation quantity: every commodity line must have a quantity, whatever its category, so it has no gate.
claims.quote:
// Every line carries a quantity, whichever category it is, so this one field
// needs no gate.

claims.statement: Obligation genus: mandatory on lines whose category asks for a genus (plants for planting, trees for planting and both hardwood categories), and out of scope otherwise.
Obligation species: mandatory on plants for planting and trees for planting lines only.
Obligation commodityCode: mandatory on every plants and wood category line, and not on potato lines.
Obligation potatoVariety: mandatory on seed and ware potato lines only.
Obligation potatoIntendedUse: mandatory on seed and ware potato lines only.
Obligation eppoCode: mandatory on plants for planting and trees for planting lines only.
Obligation sizeOfTree: mandatory on trees for planting and cut coniferous trees lines only.
Obligation phytosanitaryTreatments: mandatory on the five wood category lines only.

Each category-gated per-line obligation explains its applicability with the code obligation.{field}.applicable.becauseCategory ('{field} applies on lines whose category asks for it'), and reads its category list lazily when the gate runs.
claims.quote:
code: `obligation.${field}.applicable.becauseCategory`,
    explanation: `${field} applies on lines whose category asks for it`

claims.statement: There is no commodity catalogue or commodity search: commodity code is free text checked only for presence and length, with no lookup against the UK Trade Tariff or MDM. Looked in services/commodities/index.js, line-form.js and details.controller.js.

No maximum number of commodity lines per notification is set anywhere in the slice; only the floor of one line exists. Looked in obligations/sections/commodity.js and the list and details controllers.
No content-reviewed wording exists for any commodity page: both copy bundles are provisional and the Welsh is unreviewed machine draft, so final wording is still owed.

The slice gives no format rule for EPPO code, species or size of the trees beyond a 58-character cap, though their hints show a fixed format (a five-letter EPPO code, a binomial species name, a height in metres).
